summary: The note describes a citywide infrastructure renewal master plan announced by Mayor Linda Emerson on September 15, 2023, with rollouts by precinct through the end of 2027. It covers roads and transit, the electrical grid, water and waste systems, schools and healthcare, parks, funding, community engagement, technology and anticipated disruptions. Each area is led by a named official, and the plan is framed as a step toward a more sustainable and resilient city.
one_line: Overview of the city's infrastructure renewal master plan announced September 15, 2023, covering roads, energy, water, schools, parks, funding and the officials leading each area.
key_facts: Mayor Linda Emerson announced the infrastructure overhaul on the steps of City Hall on September 15, 2023, flanked by council members and civil engineers.
The master plan was presented at town hall meetings, with initiatives proposed by City Engineer Marcus DuBois.
Rollout timelines are set per precinct and span from late 2023 through the end of 2027.

The roads plan includes expanding key arterial roads, rehabilitating bridges that have outlived their designed lifespans, and installing intelligent traffic systems to cut congestion and make pedestrian crossings safer.
The electrical grid overhaul involves fortifying power lines, upgrading substations and integrating renewable energy, led by Energy Commissioner Anne Keating and local innovator Julian Torres.
Water Services Director Dr. Hector Mendoza is leading upgrades to outdated sewer systems and potable water pipelines to reduce leakages, ensure consistent water quality and better manage stormwater.
Council member Dr. Rebecca Sun highlights new wing additions to the General Hospital, state-of-the-art equipment, and two new K-12 schools in underserved districts.
Parks Commissioner Douglas Freeman envisions wider green corridors and more accessible parks to improve community mental and physical health.
City Treasurer Sandra Lopez proposes funding through municipal bonds, federal grants, public-private partnerships and a slight local tax increase dedicated to the projects.
Public input was gathered through participatory budgeting sessions and public forums; cafe owner James O'Reilly urged business-friendly changes.
Sarah Chan, head of the Smart City Committee, will use smart sensors, IoT applications and data analytics to monitor progress and adapt strategies in real time.
Project Director Keith Jennings warns of disruptions such as traffic detours and construction noise, requiring mitigation plans and clear communication.
